deep.reconstruction:
This page is a heavily corrected pencil draft of the opening of Section 1 ('Allgemeine Voraussetzungen und Hülfsmittel') of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). The previous page carries that title, and the next page drafts the material on connectivity (Querschnitte). The legible text corresponds closely to the printed version.

(1) Programme. To study a transcendental function, one must first set up a system of mutually independent conditions that determine it. In many cases this can be done with a principle that Dirichlet used to solve the problem for a harmonic function. The cases meant are chiefly algebraic functions, their simplest integrals and (in print) their inverse functions. In print this is 'a function of three variables satisfying Laplace's equation'. The draft has the phrase 'einen ähnlichen Gedanken von Gauss'; in print, Dirichlet was 'probably prompted by a similar idea of Gauss'.

(2) The essential new case. For transcendental functions one case matters most, and the principle in Dirichlet's form does not cover it. In that case the unknown function must take prescribed discontinuities at single points inside the domain T where it is to be determined. Riemann states precisely what this means. At each such point the function must become discontinuous like a given function discontinuous there. Equivalently, it may differ from that given function only by a function continuous at the point. The draft shows several attempts at this formulation, with many strikeouts. For this reason, he says, a presentation of the principle 'for our purpose' is needed.

(3) Set-up. A function w of x+yi is to be determined, as a function of x and y, on a surface T. It must satisfy the stated discontinuity conditions.

(4) Derivation (Cauchy-Riemann equations to Laplace equation). Put w = u + v i. The condition i ∂w/∂x = ∂w/∂y (complex differentiability) splits into two real equations. Expanding, i(u_x + i v_x) = u_y + i v_y, which gives:
- u_y = -v_x
- v_y = u_x

The elimination of v is my filling-in of the omitted step. Differentiate the second equation in x and the first in y. Then u_xx = v_yx and u_yy = -v_xy. Equality of mixed partials gives u_xx + u_yy = 0. This is the equation the page states u must satisfy.

(5) Converse. The draft notes this 'lässt sich umkehren'. If u is harmonic, then v is determined by the same equations, up to a constant, on a simply connected region. So a function of x+yi is determined through its real part.

(6) Closing lines. These are fragmentary. They say that on T, wherever the function becomes discontinuous at the given points, only real parts of functions of x+yi need be considered. They also mention a function that 'überall stetig bleibt' elsewhere. This leads into the variational (Dirichlet-integral) argument of the printed paper.

The page serves as the foundation for constructing Abelian integrals from their singularities and periods by means of the Dirichlet principle.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The only derivation is Cauchy-Riemann to Laplace, which is correct (tacitly assuming C^2 regularity, as was usual then).

The converse ('lässt sich umkehren'), recovering v from u, needs simple connectivity or period conditions. It is not justified on this page, but Riemann handles it separately via the Querschnitte on the following page.

results.what: Programme of determining a transcendental (Abelian integral) by independent conditions, via a Dirichlet-type minimum principle, extended to prescribed singularities at interior points
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle for harmonic/meromorphic functions with prescribed singularities (existence of Abelian differentials of 2nd/3rd kind)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1851 dissertation, 1857 Abelian functions); named 'Dirichlet principle' by Riemann himself, attributed to Dirichlet and Gauss

results.what: Precise definition of a prescribed discontinuity: the function differs from a given discontinuous function only by a function continuous at the point
results.modern_name: Prescribed principal parts / singular part (Mittag-Leffler-type data) for harmonic functions

results.what: Real part of an analytic function satisfies Laplace's equation, by eliminating v from the Cauchy-Riemann equations

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of the published introduction to 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857). The content, including the remark on Gauss and Dirichlet and the formulation of prescribed discontinuities, appears in print essentially verbatim. Its interest lies only in documenting drafting variants.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); u=Function('u')(x,y); v=Function('v')(x,y); w=u+I*v; expand(I*diff(w,x)-diff(w,y))
checkable.asserts: i w_x - w_y = (-v_x - u_y) + i(u_x - v_y), so the equation splits into u_y=-v_x and v_y=u_x
The real part of an analytic function (example: exp(z)) satisfies u_xx+u_yy=0
Re(1/z) is harmonic away from 0: an example of a prescribed pole-type discontinuity at an interior point

transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads: 'Als Grundlage für die Untersuchung einer Transcendenten ist es vor allem nöthig, ein System von einander unabhängiger Bestimmungen [Bedingungen] aufzustellen' (cf. printed text).

Lines 4-5: 'namentlich bei den Integralen algebraischer Functionen und ihren einfachsten / inversen Functionen, ein Princip benutzt werden' — the struck word before 'Princip/Methode' is probably 'Dirichlet'.

Line 6 likely: 'welches Dirichlet zur Lösung dieser Aufgabe für eine der Laplace'schen partiellen Differentialgleichung genügende Function ... (wahrscheinlich durch) einen ähnlichen Gedanken von Gauss veranlasst ... gegeben hat'.

Lines 8-10: 'auf welchen dieses Princip in seiner bisherigen einfachsten Form nicht anwendbar ist' and 'wenn die zu bestimmende Function in einzelnen Punkten innerhalb des Gebiets, wo sie bestimmt werden soll, vorgeschriebene Unstetigkeiten annehmen soll'.

Lines on the discontinuity condition: 'dass sie an jeder solchen Stelle unstetig werde wie eine dort gegebene unstetige Function, oder sich von ihr nur um eine an dieser Stelle stetige Function unterscheide'.
Lower middle: 'als Function von x, y in dieser Fläche T so bestimmt werden soll, dass sie den gestellten Unstetigkeitsbedingungen genügt und eine Function von x+yi ist'.
Bottom: 'die sich aus den beiden reellen Gleichungen, in welche i ∂w/∂x = ∂w/∂y zerfällt, durch Elimination von v ergiebt' — matches; the following 'Dieser Satz lässt sich umkehren'.
